g.text: Loo-Cast → Vapor: chronological history and repo-family evolution
Before the repositories: remembered origin, evidence boundary
Owner recollection: Loo-Cast begins early/mid-2021; pre-Git evidence not yet located
Remembered origin (owner says early/mid-2021; not independently verified)
Loo-Cast Legacy: Unity game, data authoring, and the first modding pressure
29109ac3 is the repo shell; 922b9c84 adds the full 793-blob Unity snapshot hours later
Substantial Unity game snapshot enters Git: 170 C# files, scenes, prefabs and assets (29109ac3 → 922b9c84)
GitHub’s 300-entry file view was capped; recursive trees confirm 793 blobs and source-level startup/linkage
9d78bbfb on June 13 is a small scene/profile/editor-state update, despite its subject
Scene and editor-state revision, not initial import (9d78bbfb)
2022: modular data, ScriptableObjects, editor drawers, gameplay growth, Steam build
Editable/modular game data and editor workflows
June 20-21: typed data is added before the complete construction/update path is connected
Station XP-drop data and typed initializer are not reached by the generic station path (6858d9ee → 2f4bc463)
Health rewrite bypasses the HUD setter and replaces serialized kill events (2f4bc463)
Jul 31: an empty Core/Object/Component and Data/RuntimeData taxonomy is tried, then removed in the next model pass
Generic data taxonomy is scaffolding with disconnected consumers and initialization contracts
Aug 3-6: generic bases are added, removed, and replaced by a new DataReference/Variable split
Runtime data extends the generic taxonomy; domain assets retain mutable state after the taxonomy rollback
Generic Core/Data bases are deleted; component-owned ScriptableObject setup and new value wrappers remain incomplete
Aug 17: data snapshots lead to asset-lifecycle JSON saves, not a shared save service; Dec 14 removes the tree
JSON persistence is coupled to ScriptableObject lifecycle and Application.dataPath, then removed (3f654f42 → 0bf0ba93 → fd6be1b6)
Oct-Nov: inventory upgrades are tried, partially repaired, then several patches are explicitly reverted
Item ownership and upgrade experiment; partial rollback
Nov 15-25: Game/save slots and a hierarchical chunk world are prototyped; observer ends as one synchronous startup sweep
Save-slot and chunk-world prototype; save path and streaming incomplete
December: worker queues, synchronous observer loading and coroutine/GPU density generation coexist
Split generation pipeline; shader layout and sampling defects visible in source
Dec 14: persisted assets are removed; save/load is explicitly not delivered on this branch
2023: modding is explicit; engine extraction and architectural experiments
d62a53a4 mod framework; 9d31582b GUDS plan; fad054e4 identifier system
Mod framework, data-system plan, stable identity pressure
January: reset action and cancellation pass expose unsafe ownership boundaries
Unconfirmed project-data deletion and broken request cancellation
February: fixed manager list, incomplete lifecycle flags and unusable BigFloat sketch
Handwired lifecycle graph and early scale-math failure
March: registries, identity, resource and data taxonomies expand; persistence ownership duplicates, then resets
Logical data and stored resource split is sketched, but both initially own recursive persistence
Concrete Data serializer throws; interface direction changes without a demonstrated conversion pipeline
Large identity/data taxonomy and manual registration are reduced in repeated framework resets
2176ae0a: Base Mod move; author describes building the chair while sitting on it
Base Mod / engine foundation built in use (2176ae0a)
941b2010 deliberately clears game code/assets so engine work can proceed
Gameplay cleared to isolate engine work (941b2010)
Engine mockup separates metadata/state/logic, then changes Enemy to components/submodules the next day
May-June: mutable data graph becomes universal hierarchy; path APIs expand, stub, and are deleted
Data, metadata and hierarchy contracts churn (selected code path review)
Registry data/metadata is called out for deletion in source, then removed in the next day's patch
Typed File/Folder/Object path APIs land with empty duplicate methods and contradictory root/absolute parsing
July: hierarchy inspector, Entity-Logic-Data, custom ECS, lifecycle and serialization overlap
Parallel runtime models accumulate adjacent responsibilities
July: BigDecimal is replaced by BigInteger/BigVec2Int for an early nested Universe prototype
Large-coordinate Universe prototype; float proximity remains
August: Unity modding branch merges, then the Unity project is replaced by Rust/Bevy
Unity-to-Rust project reset, not a direct port (52dc4a7f)
Unity mod-framework merge is discarded by the reset 13m42s later; no Unity runtime/assets survive
Rust cleanup removes the first arcade loop, leaving player movement and menus
Background exit misses all nine spawned entities
Save-slot metadata is scanned and stored, but named load only confirms the record; world restore is absent (142e9cf5 → ddbab001)
Universe save/load is deleted within an hour; empty game-configuration and plugin-group scaffolds remain (7b388def)
Save→config→state→Universe “load” chain writes empty markers; folded into synchronous loading without payload (40850c07 → 7d98cf2a)
Player observer tracks 25 empty chunk markers; recursive loading remains TODO
Rust adds local/global chunk position types; loading still installs zeroed state
Custom entity/data/logic, then ECS (87b8a852); scale, chunks, serialization, lifecycle
Engine-model experiments, ECS, scale and serialization
94fe0fd5 removes bespoke commands in favor of Lua; console/runtime integration
Runtime scripting shifts from custom commands toward Lua (94fe0fd5)
Earliest located written USF seed (e19d4f2c); concept record, not a settled contract
First USF prompt couples scale-specific model identity, event timing, DPM/ZLM detail generation, chunk residency and save-locked rules
Async chunk worker attempts do not yet execute the queued generation/load operations
Chunk-worker lifecycle advances state without doing the work
October: chunk cluster gets staged load-state types without an exposed manager API
Cluster states are private, payloads are placeholders, and manager operations are empty
November: semantic source categories feel useful, but enforcement and documentation remain implicit
Manual Rust file taxonomy makes semantic sections visible; subcategory rules stay undocumented
Nov 6-30: three residency enums, identity encodings and request queues are repeatedly replaced
Chunk/entity lifecycle splits into parallel placeholder states, then comments out its own operations
Nov: error returns and file decomposition arrive before constructor/signature integration is settled
Recoverable errors and module splitting coexist with source-visible type-shape failures
December: GlobalUniverse moves identity lookup into callers and adds a one-shot operation API
Borrowed chunk operations clarify ownership, but stale lookup types and callback dispatch do not compile together
Dec 8: root and child operations split; spawn changes a flag without issuing an ECS spawn
Lifecycle vocabulary outpaces the runtime realization path
9028dcea begins Rust crate split; build/linker and ownership friction follow
Jan 13: first Cargo split still has a template-only BaseMod and a case-mismatched workspace path
Crate boundary is declared, but the BaseMod contract and Linux path are not ready
Jan 16: BaseMod gains an Engine dependency, while old player/local chunk paths are commented out as TODOs
Crate dependency is added by disabling old chunk/entity operations before replacement is integrated
Jan 19-20: a first build/stage script repeatedly changes path ownership, then references undefined names
The managed build need is visible, but ad-hoc staging cannot reliably build and launch the workspace
Jan 22: custom managers duplicate lifecycle code; a worker wires children to root through locked trait objects
Manager startup self-deadlocks while children initialize their locked root dependency
Jan 31: native mod loader exports Rust trait objects through C ABI and drops the library handle after registration
Native mod discovery has unresolved ABI, dependency-order and code-lifetime ownership
Jan 31: Lua runs one hard-coded snippet on an unobserved worker; Engine becomes rlib while mod stays cdylib
Lua is present as an experiment, but scripting results and shared Engine ownership are unresolved
Feb 7: a custom UI object graph is added outside the declared module tree; Bevy UI remains active
Bespoke UI begins as an unregistered scaffold beside the running UI
Feb 12: the module is included, but its manager methods are empty and no plugin installs it
UI scaffold enters compilation without becoming an active UI runtime
Feb 19: Player startup stops registering the local Universe; the local processor still uses removed state inputs and direct global operations
Universe command boundary has no complete consumer wiring
Feb 17-19: old direct operations are restored, then the Player spawn path is commented out during command injection
Command API appears before its consumers replace the direct operation path
Feb 20: InfoHierarchy moves into its own module, but mutations remain in GlobalUniverse and parent/child Arcs are bidirectional
Hierarchy ownership is centralized in name but not yet in mutation; root removal can strand descendants
March-April: command proc-macro parses declarations, extracts meaning, then generates Rust; extraction is removed
Authored Rust DSL/codegen pipeline explored, then narrowed
Mar 16: broad command grammar appears while its proc-macro parser has no implementation
Command syntax is sketched before parser and generator work
Mar 21: Assets/Files modules arrive with empty serializers and an imported asset macro absent from the derive crate
Static asset vocabulary arrives without a complete declaration-to-output path
Apr 7-9: extracted metadata grows before inconsistencies and plain-String span errors are corrected
Compiler-like stages still have mismatched semantic inputs and source-level errors
May cleanup removes BaseMod/macros and Engine Game/Player/UI/Savegame; default Bevy main precedes a new chunk sandbox
Codegen/mod boundary withdrawn in prototype reset
May: registry-retained world IDs and loaded ECS entities become separate concerns, but synchronization stays manual
Registry identity meets temporary ECS realization
Mk0 directly maps coordinates to live entities; Mk1 adds eviction but its registered coordinates have no saved payload
Residency becomes bounded before persistence exists
June: conversion is replaced by upgrade code; registry rename clears all IDs and request-map removal leaves callers ill-typed
Scheduled upgrade path has a destructive registry predicate and unresolved request APIs
Mk0-Mk10 spans May 2024 through April 2025; checkpoints are resets and reversals, not releases
Prototype sequence: engine shape repeatedly reconsidered
July: event IDs become request IDs, then actor request payloads begin moving into registries
Request identity is renamed before stored-request execution is integrated
August: Lua composes Rust primitives beside a separate typed Operation prototype
Host/script composition is sketched; erased registries and broad World access remain
Aug 14: the Lua entry script uses `ops` before its initializer; Rust adds mlua without a loader
Lua composition proposal is not executable or connected to the host
August save_* names remove live registry references; they do not persist entity or actor payloads
Lifecycle naming claims more than the entity/actor save bodies implement
September: process-global request/execute/respond queue and RON chunk strings; ownership and module layout reset
Generic operations grow while world authority, durable storage, and wiring remain incomplete
Sep 6-9: Load/Unload and Save/Unsave appear, but success callbacks, durable storage and lock-safe transitions are absent
Chunk serialization is implemented in pieces, with source-level callback and self-deadlock defects
Sep 30: shared command traits and domain modules reorganize operations without closing persistence
Chunk operations move under the domain module, while facade TODOs and lifecycle defects remain
October: a static/dynamic path hierarchy is proposed as the owner of registries, commands, operations and phases
Locking hierarchy names an authority model before traversal and access enforcement work
November: typed path bindings and six lifecycle phases coexist with TODO traversal and erased command dispatch
Procedural hierarchy expands faster than its executor
Nov 30: lifecycle phases pivot to insert/remove hooks, but consumers still implement removed trait methods
Lifecycle interface migration is source-inconsistent and hierarchy execution remains stubbed
December: the hierarchy engine is archived; chunk streaming and Lua task composition return in a smaller prototype
Chunk ownership reset with Lua tasks; retry state is fragmented
Dec 14-19: task scripts are present, but active engine wiring and syntax do not match the declared Lua runtime
Lua task files are disconnected from the active engine; scripts are not valid Lua 5.4 as written
January: action buffers centralize some work, but retries and per-frame cost remain unresolved
Chunk actions gain a budget; lifecycle and completion remain incomplete
Jan 9-13: Mk5 adds an unscheduled manager candidate while the plugin retains the removed retry path
Chunk ownership migration is split between an incomplete candidate and source-inconsistent scheduled code
February-March: workflows span ECS/async/render; macros take over generated stage code
Typed-looking staged workflows use erased IO and churn through event bridges
April: wait/setup/completion/failure become explicit; bounded channels and schedule ordering expose lifecycle assumptions
Workflow lifecycle is clearer, but instance ownership and global channel lifecycle remain unresolved
May: chunk workflows batch real work, but queue removal precedes completion; captured async context gains invocation identity and lifecycle debt
Chunk-action workflow integration and composite capture remain lossy/coarse-grained
June: intent resolution/commit stays incomplete; a custom tracing viewer starts, then forks into duplicate unfinished storage
Action authority and observability split into separate incomplete experiments
July: logger tree and selection APIs churn; the console paints virtually but eagerly gathers unbounded history
Typed trace paths outpace safe extraction and scalable log retention
August: Bevy migration, time ownership churn, and chunk-debug dock expand into an inspector workbench
Inspector/workbench direction appears before time and editor contracts settle
September: USF scale moves from multiplying static types toward runtime scale and ChunkCoord; crate boundaries churn; multiplayer is deferred
USF becomes explicit, but scale arithmetic and engine/mod loading contracts remain unsettled
Mk9 checkpoint deprioritizes multiplayer and names modding + USF as the next focus
Modding and USF become explicit next focus
October 2025-June 2026: glossary recovery, issue structure, and design authority are revisited
Architecture vocabulary and historical design records accumulate
October: nested Grid/Subgrid/Unit coordinates and camera-driven chart transitions; f32 conversion and transition ownership remain open

November: render/camera ownership consolidates; transform projection stays schedule-sensitive, custom picking/readback remains experimental
Logical/render synchronization and debug picking have no complete shared bridge yet
December: position equality normalizes nested charts; coord and render origin diverge; wrapping returns to local constants
Spatial values gain names and equality while their update authority remains distributed
January 2026: Rhai hooks expose the temporary-capability idea, implemented through erased Rust lifetimes and runtime teardown conventions

March: finite Rust signatures become the execution boundary; Rhai begins registering typed USF content

USF design reset and process rails begin; math facade is not operational

Process becomes explicit while the numeric experiment remains unsettled
June: raw owner answers, provenance labels, glossary corrections and architecture ownership are made explicit
Intent and implementation evidence gain separate authority
June 16: capability semantics are explicitly pressure-tested, not frozen

Follow-up answers define authored projections and automatic composition, while preserving unanswered boundaries

Enginepack/Gamepack/Modpack and ExtensionMod inheritance become the provisional composition vocabulary
